title: PROJECT_PLAN Schema
description: Project execution plan schema for PM Agent output. PM Agent is the orchestrator that analyzes TECH_SPEC, creates phases with task skeletons, defines maturity gates, and controls the fleet of specialized agents (Task Generation, Task Execution).

projectName.description: Name of the project (must match TECH_SPEC)

projectContext.description: High-level project context derived from TECH_SPEC

techSpecRef.description: Path to the TECH_SPEC.json file that this plan is based on

architectureSummary.description: Brief summary of system architecture from TECH_SPEC
examples: Modular monolith with Node.js/Express/TypeScript, PostgreSQL database, REST APIs with clear service boundaries for future microservices migration
Microservices architecture with event-driven communication via Kafka, polyglot persistence

maturityModel.description: Maturity-based execution model for parallelization strategy

levels.description: Maturity levels from sequential to full parallel

examples: Foundation building - high interdependency, sequential only
Stable base established - 2-3 parallel streams safe
Mature system - multiple independent features can be developed in parallel

parallelizationCapacity.description: How many parallel streams are safe at this level

currentLevel.description: Current maturity level of the project

technologyStack.description: Key technology choices from TECH_SPEC (for quick reference)

examples: Jest with TDD workflow, 90%+ coverage target

phases.description: Execution phases with task skeletons. PM Agent decides phase grouping based on TECH_SPEC critical path and feature dependencies.

features.description: MVP features covered in this phase (from in-scope.md or RefinedIDEA)

maturityLevel.description: Maturity level for this phase (determines parallelization safety)

dependencies.description: Array of phaseIds that must complete before this phase can start

criticalPath.description: Whether this phase is on the critical path for MVP (from TECH_SPEC)

maturityGate.description: Exit criteria that must be met before proceeding to next phase. Combines TECH_SPEC NFRs + phase-specific checks (Q3: Option C).

nfrChecks.description: Non-functional requirements from TECH_SPEC that apply to this phase

securityChecks.description: Security requirements that must be verified

examples: JWT token generation and validation working
User registration and login flows complete
Integration tests with User Service passing

integrationTestsPassing.description: Whether integration tests must pass for this phase gate

buildSuccessful.description: Whether build must succeed for this phase gate

taskSkeletons.description: Lightweight task skeletons for this phase. Task Generation Agent will convert these into comprehensive TASK_OBJECTS.

title.description: Brief task title (usually endpoint or feature component)

feature.description: Which MVP feature this task belongs to

scope.description: Brief description of what needs to be built (1-3 sentences)
examples: Implement user profile retrieval endpoint with sports preferences JOIN. Include authentication middleware and field-level access control.
Create team creation endpoint with captain assignment. Handle team validation, database persistence, and initial team_members entry.

requirements.description: Business rules and acceptance criteria (not implementation details)
examples: JOIN users with user_sports table to include sports preferences
Filter email/phone for other users' profiles (own profile shows all)
Captain must be a valid registered user
Team name must be unique per sport
Auto-create team_members entry for captain with is_captain=true
Support multiple sports (pickleball, paddle, basketball, etc.)

complexity.description: Estimated complexity for Task Generation Agent

dependencies.description: Array of taskIds that must complete before this task

context.description: Architectural context from TECH_SPEC for Task Generation Agent

technologyStack.description: Relevant tech stack for this task

examples: TDD with 90%+ coverage (unit, integration, e2e, regression)
BDD with Cucumber and contract testing
JWT authentication with bcrypt password hashing, input validation with Zod

executionStrategy.description: Overall execution strategy for the project

recommendedStartPhase.description: Which phase to start development with

parallelizationGuidance.description: When and how to safely parallelize development based on maturity model
examples: Start with P1 sequentially (foundation). After P1 gate passes, P2 can proceed sequentially. Once P2 gate passes with 90%+ coverage and stable interfaces, controlled parallelization (2-3 streams) is safe for P3-P5.
P1-P2 must be sequential (critical dependencies). P3+ can be fully parallelized after P2 maturity gate.

integrationCheckpoints.description: Points where cross-phase integration should be verified

afterPhase.description: Phase ID after which to run integration check

checkDescription.description: What to verify at this checkpoint
examples: Verify User Service auth integration with all endpoints
Verify Team Service integration with User Service (team members, captain validation)
Verify Match Service integration with User and Team Services

taskGenerationStrategy.description: When and how PM Agent invokes Task Generation Agent
examples: Generate tasks for P1 immediately. Generate P2-P3 tasks after P1 gate passes. Generate P4+ tasks on-demand.
Generate all phase tasks upfront for comprehensive planning.
Generate tasks phase-by-phase as development progresses.

unstructuredNotes.description: Freeform notes from PM Agent about execution strategy, risks, trade-offs, or context for Task Generation Agent and Task Execution Agents.
examples: Critical: User Service (P1) and Team Service (P2) are foundational - DO NOT parallelize. These must achieve 90%+ coverage before any parallelization. Match Service (P3) has complex business rules around result verification - Task Generation Agent should create comprehensive edge case tests. Stats Service (P4) can be parallelized with League/Tournament services once Match Service is stable. Watch for N+1 query problems in leaderboard calculations - may need Redis optimization.
